claims.text: As-fabricated stainless steel has insufficient corrosion resistance in extreme corrosive environments.
Machine-learning-guided optimization of laser cladding parameters will create a tailored surface microstructure on stainless steel.
The tailored surface microstructure will significantly improve corrosion resistance relative to untreated stainless steel.
The tailored surface microstructure will significantly improve corrosion resistance relative to conventionally treated stainless steel.
A predictive machine-learning framework based on historical experimental data can optimize laser power, deposition speed, and layer thickness for laser cladding.
Optimized laser cladding will produce an engineered surface layer with a refined microstructure.
Optimized laser cladding will produce secondary phases whose formation and distribution can be predicted by the machine-learning model.
The secondary phases in the engineered layer act as barriers to corrosive species.
The optimized laser cladding parameters promote a fine and uniform grain structure.
The optimized laser cladding parameters promote strategically distributed secondary phases.
The modified surface impedes corrosion by reducing pathways available to corrosive species.
Machine-learning-guided laser-clad stainless steel will exhibit lower corrosion rates and weight loss than untreated and conventionally laser-clad samples.
Machine-learning-guided laser-clad stainless steel will exhibit improved electrochemical impedance responses relative to untreated and conventionally laser-clad samples.
